title: Unwrapping the Dial: Frontier Semantics, Measured Ticks and Ranked Scale Labellings for Training-Free Instrument Reading with Black-Box VLMs

sub_topic: Perceptual blind spots of frontier vision-language models
Analog instrument and clock reading (visual measurement reading)
Training-free tool augmentation of black-box VLMs
primary_focus: Moving the fine-grained measurement out of the frontier model's lossy encoder-to-language readout and into locally measured geometry
Jointly ranked labelling hypotheses (numeral-to-tick, tick-count, hand-role) with a margin that serves as an abstention signal independent of the frontier model
A committed, pilot-gated accuracy and cost change on MeasureBench real dials and TickTockVQA under a modest API budget

one_sentence_thesis: Let the frontier model read what a dial's numbers and hands mean, measure every angle from the photo's own ticks, and pick the scale labelling that best explains both.

core_problem.problem_statement: Frontier VLMs read the unit and the rough scale of an analog dial correctly but get the value wrong: the best reported model is right on 31.5% of MeasureBench real dials while getting the unit right 96.2% of the time, and extra thinking tokens give very little improvement [2510.26865]. The needed signal, the exact angle of a few-pixel needle relative to a periodic tick ring, is lost in the model's visual readout, while trained geometric pipelines that do measure it break on unseen dial designs [2510.26865][2404.08785][2511.21982].
why_it_matters: Reading gauges, meters and clocks is a basic industrial-inspection and assistive task, and 2026 frontier models still fail it: on a uniform real dial they reach about 14% normalised MAE while reading an in-band digital display almost perfectly [2604.22829].

The failure is a readout failure, not a knowledge failure: models identify the instrument, unit and major spacing but miss by one or more ticks, frontier API models answer '10:10' on 11.9-29.7% of real clocks, and do not improve with reasoning [2510.26865]; Astra-style higher reasoning effort costs up to 13.22x and does not close fine-geometry gaps [2609.35718].

Every black-box remedy studied so far still ends with the frontier model reading pixels (prompts, hints, visual prompts) [2407.06581][2603.16250][2605.16410][2610.12942], and arbiters that decide whether to trust a tool use the same blind model as the reference [2610.04836][2512.06373].

Trained dial readers modify weights and stay near or below the frontier on real dials (TriSCA 28.5% vs 31.5%) [2604.26614], DialBench's reader 'struggles to predict well on meter images it has never seen before' [2511.21982], and synthetic-data training transfers weakly to real images [2510.26865][2603.08011].
core_problem.concrete_example: A photo of an ammeter whose pointer sits on 20 A: GPT-5 answers 26 A with the correct unit [2510.26865]. The Reitsma modular reader, which anchors the scale on OCR'd numerals, detects only 18-35% of scale markers and so fails to produce a usable scale on 40-57.5% of images [2404.08785]. On a real wall clock showing 4:37 the frontier model answers '10:10', the output prior MeasureBench reports for 20.34% of GPT-5's real-clock answers [2510.26865], and a Hough line fit returns two unlabelled lines that may be read with hour and minute swapped [2603.08011].

key_novelty.main_idea: Labelling-ranked dial unwrapping: frontier-read semantics as the coarse code, the photo's own tick lattice as the fine measurement, and a needle-only counterfactual sweep
explanation: Like a structured-light scanner, the coarse signal (numeral values, the frontier's semantics) only picks which interval; the fine signal (measured tick and needle angles) supplies the value.

Instead of rounding level by level, all neighbouring scale labellings (numeral one tick over, a missed tick, swapped hands) are scored together; the winner's lead over the runner-up says when to abstain.
The needle is found by pasting candidate needle silhouettes onto the photo: at the true angle the paste changes almost nothing in frozen features, so shadows and counterweights are rejected.

problem_definition.formal_setting: Given an image I of an analog instrument with K>=1 pointers and a question q, recover the reading y (value and unit). Model the dial after rectification as a pivot c, a set of tick angles T={t_1<...<t_N} with radial lengths l_i, numeral boxes B={(b_j, alpha_j)} with angular positions alpha_j, and pointer angles phi_1..phi_K. The reading is y = V_h(phi), where V_h maps an angle to a value under a labelling hypothesis h = (pi, c, d, rho): pi assigns numeral boxes to major-tick indices, c inserts or deletes at most one tick per major interval, d is the scale direction and rho assigns pointer roles (hour/minute/second, or decade order on multi-dial meters). The frontier model F, a black box, returns per-box values v_j, the unit u, the scale type s (linear, non-linear, multiple scales) and pointer semantics, but never angles. We seek h* = argmax_h S(h; T, B, v, phi) and the margin m = S(h*) - max{S(h): |V_h(phi) - V_h*(phi)| exceeds the answer tolerance}; output y if m >= tau, otherwise abstain and fall back to F's own reading. Correctness of the numeral-to-tick assignment by nearest major tick requires |alpha_j - theta_pi(j)| < Delta_major/2, the dial analogue of the half-period condition of multi-frequency phase unwrapping [1903.09836].
problem_definition.inputs: One RGB image of an analog dial instrument (single-pointer gauge, multi-hand clock, or multi-dial electricity meter) and a natural-language reading question; API access to one frontier VLM (GPT-6 Astra) used once per image at default reasoning effort; frozen local models on one 24 GB GPU.
problem_definition.outputs: The reading in the instrument's unit (or h:mm for clocks), a reliability margin m, a needle-peak sharpness score, an abstain flag, and the intermediate evidence (labelled tick lattice, numeral-to-tick assignment, needle angle) that can optionally be handed back to the frontier model.

key_terms.coarse code: Information that is imprecise but unambiguous about which interval the reading lies in: the values of the printed numerals, the unit, the scale type and which hand is which. Here it is read by the frontier model.
key_terms.fine phase: Precise but periodic measurements: the angles of every tick and of the needle, measured from the photo. A tick is easy to locate but by itself does not say which tick it is.
key_terms.labelling hypothesis: One complete guess of how the measured ticks are numbered: which major tick each numeral belongs to, whether a tick was missed or spurious, and which pointer has which role.
key_terms.joint ranking: Scoring all neighbouring labelling hypotheses together rather than fixing one level at a time, so that an early mistake (a numeral attached to the wrong tick) cannot silently propagate.
key_terms.margin: How much better the best labelling explains the evidence than the best rival that would change the answer; a small margin triggers abstention.
key_terms.paste-and-compare needle sweep: Rendering a needle silhouette at a candidate angle onto the photo and measuring how much frozen image features change; at the true needle position the paste is almost a no-op.
key_terms.half-interval condition: A numeral attaches to the right major tick if its measured position is off by less than half the spacing between major ticks; the dial version of the rule that makes phase unwrapping exact.
key_terms.hybrid A: Baseline: frontier semantics plus a Reitsma-style linear angle-to-value fit through numeral positions plus a Hough/line needle.
key_terms.hybrid B: Baseline: frontier semantics plus this paper's ranked tick lattice plus a Hough/line needle; it isolates the contribution of the needle sweep.
key_terms.coverage: The fraction of images on which the method answers instead of abstaining.

related_work.sub_area: Frontier VLM evaluation on measurement reading and hard vision
related_work.what_it_does: MeasureBench scores 18 VLMs on 1,272 real instrument images by per-image value intervals; the best model reaches 31.5% on 711 real dials with 96.2% unit accuracy, thinking barely helps, clocks and multi-needle dials are hardest, and errors include one-minor-tick misses, whole-interval misses (26 A for 20 A) and a '10:10' output prior [2510.26865]. The dynamic-gauge study finds 2026 frontier models fail real gauges but read digits near-perfectly and recommends VLMs for semantics plus deterministic geometry for the needle [2604.22829]. The GPT-6 Astra evaluation shows higher reasoning effort and built-in tools close some gaps at 1.04-13.22x cost, but metric, fine-boundary and small-structure gaps remain [2609.35718].
related_work.open_gap: These are diagnoses. None builds the recommended semantics-plus-geometry division of labour as a training-free method on a broad real-image benchmark, and Astra itself has not been measured on dials.

related_work.what_it_does: TriSCA aligns a 4B VLM's visual tower on 400K synthetic triplets, then applies SFT and real-image GRPO, lifting Qwen3-VL-4B from 12.0% to 28.5% on MeasureBench real dials [2604.26614]. DialBench's MRLM injects CLIP template features of meter archetypes via cross-attention and MoE, trained end to end on RPM-10K [2511.21982]. Swap-DPO fine-tunes VLMs on TickTockVQA with hour/minute-swapped negatives built from the angle coupling theta_h = 30h + m/2 [2603.08011]. A synthetic-only CNN classifies start, end and needle angles with 2-5 degree error on real gauges [2308.14583].
related_work.open_gap: All modify weights, so none can help an API-only frontier model; they generalise poorly to unseen designs [2511.21982] and stay near the frontier's own accuracy on real dials [2604.26614]. The clock-hand coupling is used only to build training negatives, never as an inference-time consistency check [2603.08011].

related_work.what_it_does: Reitsma et al. detect the gauge, find major notches with a trained DINOv2 keypoint head, fit an ellipse, OCR numerals with DBNet+ABINet, fit a RANSAC linear angle-to-value map through numeral angles and intersect a segmented needle line; error is 0.77-1.15% of range when OCR reads two or more numerals, but OCR fails on 40-57.5% of images [2404.08785]. MeterFL segments ticks and pointer with a trained 30.6M U-Net, unwraps them into a polar strip and counts ticks from the scale start with v_min and delta_v supplied, reaching 87.2% within two minor divisions [2609.31998].
related_work.open_gap: Reitsma interpolates linearly between numerals and ignores minor ticks, assumes linear scales and breaks at OCR and needle segmentation (shadows, white-on-white); MeterFL needs metadata it does not read and counts from the start, so one missed tick shifts every later index. Neither ranks alternative labellings or abstains on a calibrated margin, and both were built around trained components that overfit (8.5% on MeasureBench real images for Reitsma) [2510.26865].

related_work.what_it_does: FoundPose estimates unseen-object pose without training by matching frozen DINOv2 ViT-L layer-18 patch descriptors between a real crop and renders of an exact textured 3D model, with bag-of-words template retrieval and featuremetric refinement; intermediate-layer patches carry positional information that the cls token lacks [2311.18809].
related_work.open_gap: It assumes an exact 3D model and a good mask; it has not been used for a 2D low-parameter shape such as a needle, where the model space is small enough to enumerate.

related_work.what_it_does: Temporal phase unwrapping recovers the integer fringe order by rounding the scaled coarse-minus-fine phase, correct only while the combined error stays below half a period, which forces hierarchical unwrapping when the frequency ratio is large [1903.09836]. Kinect-style multi-frequency ToF replaces sequential CRT unwrapping, which propagates early errors, with joint enumeration and ranking of all plausible unwrapping vectors, and reuses the winner's density as a single outlier-rejection confidence (about 52% more valid measurements) [1608.05209].
related_work.open_gap: Never applied to reading instruments. On a dial the whole lattice is visible, so the transferable part is not period counting but the joint enumeration of neighbouring labellings and the margin used as an abstention signal.

related_work.sub_area: Black-box remedies for VLM perceptual blind spots and tool-trust arbitration
related_work.what_it_does: Prompting, CoT and slow thinking do not fix low-level perception even though frozen-encoder probes recover it [2407.06581]; task-wise visual prompts still leave the black-box VLM reading the edited pixels [2603.16250]; learned hints [2605.16410] and visual demonstrations [2610.12942] steer but do not add perception. Tool-trust arbiters use the same backbone VLM to verify specialist outputs [2610.04836] or a trained rethink turn bounded by the model's own grounding [2512.06373].
related_work.open_gap: No black-box method hands the frontier model an answer-bearing measurement with a reliability signal that does not pass through the frontier's own visual readout.

related_work.what_it_does: DBNet is a real-time segmentation-based detector for multi-oriented and curved scene text, ResNet-18 variant at 48-62 FPS, trained on generic scene text [1911.08947]. Grounding DINO detects arbitrary text-named categories zero-shot (52.5 AP on COCO without COCO data; 172M parameters for the Swin-T variant) but can hallucinate false positives [2303.05499].
related_work.open_gap: Used here as frozen, benchmark-agnostic components: DBNet localises numerals (the frontier only reads their values), Grounding DINO crops dials; neither is trained on any dial data.

high_level_flow: Localise: Grounding DINO dial crop -> ellipse rectification and pivot estimate -> DBNet numeral boxes
Ask once: numbered-box overlay -> single frontier call (box values, unit, scale type, minors per major, pointer semantics, own reading)
Measure: polar unwrap of the rectified annulus -> tick lattice with major/minor split
Label: enumerate neighbouring labelling hypotheses -> joint scoring -> winner + margin
Locate pointer(s): full-range paste-and-compare silhouette sweep on frozen DINOv2 patches -> native-resolution refinement between flanking ticks -> clock-hand / decade coupling check
Answer: value from local interval interpolation -> abstain or answer -> optional evidence hand-back to the frontier

modules.role: Crop each dial face and map it to a fronto-parallel circle with a known pivot.
modules.model: Grounding DINO-T (Swin-T, 172M) frozen, prompt 'gauge dial . clock face . meter dial' [2303.05499]; classical ellipse fit (RANSAC on radial edge points)
modules.notes: MeasureBench images are mostly tight instrument photos, so the detector is used only when the dial covers less than about half of the image or when several dials are present (electricity meters). The ellipse is fitted to the outer ring of high-gradient radial structures; the pivot is refined as the point that minimises the spread of line-segment directions through the hub region. Grounding DINO's stated false positives [2303.05499] are filtered by requiring a fitted ellipse with tick-like periodic structure.

modules.role: Find where the scale numerals are, without reading them.
modules.model: DBNet ResNet-18, off-the-shelf scene-text weights, frozen [1911.08947]
outputs: numeral boxes b_j with angle alpha_j and radius r_j about the pivot
modules.notes: Follows the reviewer's carry-forward: positions come from a local detector, never from the frontier model, whose named limit is fine-grained spatial grounding [2510.26865]. Boxes far from the dominant numeral radius are kept but flagged (serial numbers, brand text) so the frontier can label them 'not a scale numeral'. Reitsma's pipeline found only 18-35% of markers with detection plus recognition combined [2404.08785]; the pilot reports detection recall alone.

modules.role: Read the semantics the frontier is good at: numeral values, unit, scale type, minor divisions per major, pointer roles and rotation directions.
modules.model: GPT-6 Astra through its API, default reasoning effort, one call per image
inputs: rectified crop with numbered box outlines drawn on it
structured prompt with a JSON answer schema
outputs: value v_j or 'not a scale numeral' per box id
decade order and rotation direction for multi-dial meters
the frontier's own reading y_F (used only as fallback and diagnostic)
modules.notes: Unit reading is the frontier's strongest sub-skill (96.2%) [2510.26865] and digit reading is near-perfect [2604.22829]. The frontier's reading y_F is NOT used to centre any search window and does NOT enter the margin: it can be a whole major interval off or stuck at 10:10 [2510.26865][2604.26614]. Per-call cost and latency are logged for every call.

modules.role: Measure every tick angle and length from the photo.
modules.model: Training-free: polar unwrap of the annulus between 0.6 and 1.0 rim radius into a 1440 x 128 strip, per-column contrast against a median face profile, 1D peak detection, 2-means clustering of radial extent into major/minor; optional variant: 30.6M U-Net trained on MeterFL masks [2609.31998]
modules.notes: Polar unwrapping follows MeterFL [2609.31998] but at twice its angular resolution and without its trained segmenter in the main path. When the optional segmenter is used the claim becomes 'nothing is trained on the benchmark' rather than 'nothing is trained'. Minor ticks are counted locally between two measured majors, so a missed tick corrupts one interval instead of shifting every later index as in MeterFL's count-from-start decoder.

modules.role: Choose the scale labelling that best explains numerals, lattice and pointer together, and measure how decisive that choice is.
modules.model: Exhaustive enumeration over a small discrete space plus a hand-specified log-score; no learned parameters
modules.notes: Hypotheses: for each numeral the nearest major tick and its two neighbours; per major interval an insertion or deletion of at most one minor tick; both scale directions; all pointer-role permutations. Joint enumeration follows the ToF unwrapping argument that sequential rounding propagates early errors while joint ranking checks the true maximum [1608.05209]. The margin is computed only against rivals that change the answer beyond the tolerance, so harmless ambiguities do not cause abstention. Non-linear scales attach values to tick indices and interpolate piecewise, so no global angle model is needed (Reitsma excluded non-linear dials [2404.08785]).

modules.role: Locate each pointer angle robustly to shadows, glare gaps, counterweights and tapered or hollow hands.
modules.model: DINOv2 ViT-L/14 frozen, layer-18 patch descriptors as in FoundPose [2311.18809]; 2D silhouette renderer with 12 shape variants
inputs: pointer colour sampled near the hub
angular range: full scale arc on gauges, full circle on clocks and meter sub-dials
modules.notes: For each candidate angle and variant, the silhouette (taper, tail or counterweight length, hub radius, width) is composited onto the photo; the score is the mean cosine similarity of layer-18 descriptors between photo and composite on the patches the silhouette touches. At the true pose the paste is nearly a no-op. Coarse pass at 2 degrees with 3 generic variants, then top-3 peaks refined at 0.25 degrees with all 12 variants, then sub-pixel tip refinement against the two flanking measured ticks at native resolution. The window is never centred on the frontier reading (reviewer carry-forward). For clocks the sweep is over the 720 joint (hour, minute) states, which fixes both hand angles by theta_h = 30h + m/2 [2603.08011]; an independent per-hand sweep is also run, and disagreement between the two lowers the margin.

modules.role: Turn the labelled lattice and the pointer angle into a value, decide whether to answer, and optionally return evidence to the frontier.
modules.notes: y = V_h*(t_i) + (phi - t_i)/(t_{i+1} - t_i) * (V_h*(t_{i+1}) - V_h*(t_i)) for the flanking ticks t_i, t_{i+1}, the local form of MeterFL's interpolation [2609.31998]. Multi-dial meters use decade coupling: a higher-decade pointer's fraction within its digit must agree with the lower-decade reading, a direct use of the coarse-phase constraint [1903.09836]. Abstain if m < tau_m or sharpness < tau_s, thresholds fixed on the pilot split only; on abstention the system returns y_F flagged as unverified, so accuracy at 100% coverage is always reported.

novel_architectural_elements: The frontier model is placed only on the semantic branch (values of locally detected boxes, unit, scale type, pointer roles) and never on a geometric quantity; every angle comes from local measurement.
Numeral values, tick lattice and pointer angles meet in one joint hypothesis space instead of a pipeline of hard decisions, and its margin is the system's sole reliability output.
The needle search is a full-range sweep of counterfactual composites scored in a frozen encoder's patch space, coupled to the labelling ranking through the hand-role and decade constraints.
method.pseudocode:
def read_dial(I, q, F):
    dials = detect_and_rectify(I)                 # Grounding DINO-T + ellipse fit
    out = []
    for D in dials:
        boxes = dbnet(D.crop)                     # positions only
        sem = F.call(I, overlay(D.crop, boxes), schema=COARSE_CODE)  # one API call per image
        ticks = tick_lattice(polar_unwrap(D.crop, D.pivot), sem.minors_per_major)
        rng = full_circle if sem.kind in {'clock', 'meter_subdial'} else scale_arc(ticks)
        cands = needle_sweep(D.crop, D.pivot, rng, variants=12, feat=dinov2_l18)  # top-3 peaks
        H = enumerate_labellings(boxes, sem.values, ticks, sem.scale_type, sem.roles, cands)
        scores = {h: S(h) for h in H}             # numerals + lattice + values + coupling
        h_star = argmax(scores)
        y = interpolate_local(h_star, refine_tip(cands[h_star.pointer], ticks))
        rivals = [h for h in H if abs(value(h) - y) > tol(sem)]
        m = scores[h_star] - max(scores[h] for h in rivals)
        out.append((y, m, sharpness(cands)))
    y, m, s = combine(out, sem)                   # decade coupling for multi-dial meters
    if m < TAU_M or s < TAU_S:
        return sem.own_reading, ABSTAIN
    return (y, sem.unit), ANSWER
design_choices: Frontier reads values but not positions: its unit and digit reading are strong [2510.26865][2604.22829] while fine spatial grounding is its named limit [2510.26865]; this also removes Reitsma's dominant OCR-recognition failure [2404.08785].

Joint ranking rather than level-by-level rounding: sequential unwrapping propagates early errors and joint enumeration guarantees the true labelling is checked [1608.05209]; this is presented as a recombination with phase unwrapping, not a deep analogy, because the whole lattice is visible on a dial.

Local interval interpolation on measured minor ticks rather than a global linear fit through numerals: a 1-2% of range interpolation error is about one minor division [2404.08785], which is MeasureBench's failure tolerance [2510.26865].

Full-range needle sweep rather than a window around the frontier reading: frontier readings can be a whole major interval off or collapse to 10:10 [2510.26865], so a frontier-centred window would systematically miss the needle.

Silhouette paste-and-compare in frozen layer-18 DINOv2 patches rather than a line fit: intermediate patches carry the positional information needed to read a geometric state without training [2311.18809], and an asymmetric silhouette resolves the tip/tail ambiguity Reitsma settles by heuristic [2404.08785].
Abstention independent of the frontier: the margin uses only local evidence, because VLM-derived confidence signals fail exactly where perception fails [2610.04836][2512.06373].

No training in the main path, so the method cannot overfit training designs, the failure that made trained pipelines collapse on MeasureBench [2510.26865]; the optional MeterFL-trained segmenter is reported as a separate variant.
method.theoretical_grounding: In multi-frequency unwrapping the fringe order k = round(((f_h/f_l)Phi_l - phi_h)/2pi) is exact iff the combined phase error stays below half an order [1903.09836, Eq 8-11]. On a dial the analogous statement is: nearest-major assignment of numeral j is correct iff |alpha_j - theta_true(j)| < Delta_major/2. Dial hierarchies have ratios of 2, 5 or 10 minors per major, well below the roughly 16-period single-step limit reported for MF-TPU [1903.09836], so the condition is loose (about 13-27 degrees on common gauges). With n >= 2 numerals and a monotone, value-consistent assignment constraint, a wrong labelling requires several numerals to violate the condition in the same direction, which the joint score penalises. The margin m is a log-likelihood ratio between the best and best answer-changing labelling; thresholding it is the dial analogue of the single density threshold that replaced five hand-tuned filters in ToF unwrapping [1608.05209]. These are design arguments, not proofs; the pilot measures whether the condition actually holds on real web photos.

model_details.base_model: No model is trained or fine-tuned in the main method. Frozen components: GPT-6 Astra (black-box API, default effort, one call per image); DINOv2 ViT-L/14 layer-18 patch descriptors [2311.18809]; DBNet ResNet-18 with public scene-text weights [1911.08947]; Grounding DINO-T (Swin-T, 172M) [2303.05499]. Optional variant: a 30.6M-parameter U-Net tick/pointer segmenter as in MeterFL [2609.31998].

training.method: No model training for the main method (training-free inference with hand-specified scores). Optional variant only: supervised segmentation of tick and pointer masks on the public MeterFL masks, never on MeasureBench or TickTockVQA images.
objective_functions: Purpose: pick the scale labelling that best explains numerals, ticks and pointers. Formally: S(h) = sum_j log N(alpha_j - theta_pi(j); 0, sigma_n^2) + lambda_1 sum_k log p(n_k | M, rho_k) + lambda_2 log p(V_h | s) + lambda_3 log p(phi | rho, coupling), where n_k is the corrected minor count in major interval k, M the frontier-stated minors per major, rho_k the spacing regularity, p(V_h | s) rewards arithmetic (linear) or monotone (non-linear) value progressions, and the coupling term enforces theta_h = 30h + m/2 on clocks or decade consistency on meters.

Purpose: locate the pointer as the pose at which pasting a needle changes the image least. Formally: phi* = argmax_{phi, s} (1/|P(phi,s)|) sum_{p in P(phi,s)} cos(f_18(I)_p, f_18(I composited with silhouette(phi, s))_p), with P(phi,s) the patches the silhouette touches and f_18 frozen DINOv2 layer-18 descriptors.

Purpose: decide when to answer. Formally: answer iff m = S(h*) - max_{h: |V_h(phi) - V_h*(phi)| > tol} S(h) >= tau_m and sharpness >= tau_s, with tau chosen on the pilot split to maximise accuracy at the frontier-fallback operating point.
Purpose (optional segmenter only): learn tick and pointer masks. Formally: L = L_CE(mask_pred, mask_gt) + L_Dice(mask_pred, mask_gt) on MeterFL training masks.
training.adaptation: None for the main method; optional segmenter trained from scratch (full training, 30.6M parameters) in a few GPU-hours on one RTX 4090.

key_hyperparameters.polar_strip: 1440 angular bins x 128 radial bins over 0.6-1.0 rim radius
key_hyperparameters.needle_sweep: coarse 2 deg with 3 variants; refine top-3 peaks at 0.25 deg with 12 variants; full scale arc on gauges, full circle on clocks and meter sub-dials
key_hyperparameters.dinov2_input: 448 px rectified crop, layer 18 of ViT-L/14
key_hyperparameters.labelling_neighbourhood: numeral-to-major offset in {-1,0,+1}; at most one minor insertion or deletion per major interval; both directions; all pointer-role permutations
key_hyperparameters.sigma_n: one quarter of the measured major-tick spacing
key_hyperparameters.lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3, tau_m, tau: set on the pilot split only, then frozen for all test runs
key_hyperparameters.optional_segmenter: U-Net 30.6M, Adam lr 1e-3, 100 epochs on MeterFL masks

related_methods: GPT-6 Astra alone: frontier VLM at default, high and xhigh reasoning effort, optionally with its built-in Python/crop tools [2609.35718].
Gemini-2.5-Pro on MeasureBench: best published 31.5% on real dials (2025 figure) [2510.26865].
TriSCA: three-stage trained Qwen3-VL-4B, 28.5% on MeasureBench real dials [2604.26614].
Reitsma et al.: modular trained gauge reader with OCR numeral anchoring, 8.5% on MeasureBench real images [2404.08785][2510.26865].
MeterFL pipeline: trained U-Net tick segmentation with polar unwrapping and metadata-supplied tick counting [2609.31998].
DialBench MRLM: end-to-end trained pointer-meter VLM with template cross-attention [2511.21982].
Swap-DPO on TickTockVQA: LoRA SFT + DPO clock reader [2603.08011].
SEVEX: searched task-wise visual prompts for a black-box VLM [2603.16250].
key_differences: vs. Astra with more effort or built-in tools: the frontier never reads an angle; one default-effort call supplies only semantics, so the cost does not scale with reasoning effort.
vs. TriSCA, DialBench and Swap-DPO: no weights are changed and no dial data is trained on, so the method applies to an API-only model and cannot overfit training designs.

vs. Reitsma: the frontier replaces OCR recognition, a local detector supplies positions, readings come from measured minor ticks rather than linear interpolation between numerals, non-linear scales need no global model, and a silhouette replaces the symmetric line fit plus 'closer end' heuristic.

vs. MeterFL: v_min, delta_v and tick values are read by the frontier rather than supplied, minors are counted locally between measured majors, and alternative labellings are ranked with a margin instead of a single deterministic count from the scale start.
vs. SEVEX and other visual prompting: the answer-bearing measurement is computed locally and handed over, rather than the frontier reading edited pixels.
vs. RSure-style or rethink-turn arbitration: the reliability signal (labelling margin and needle sharpness) never uses the frontier's own visual reading.

proposed_evaluation.evaluation_setting: Single-image analog reading with a black-box frontier VLM (GPT-6 Astra) as the system being helped, under the paper's constraints: all experiments finish by 2026-11-09, total API spend at most about US$1,000, local compute on one RTX 4090 (24 GB). Timeline: 2026-10-19 to 10-25 build the pipeline using only TickTockVQA train images and MeterFL for debugging, and hand-annotate major-tick angles, numeral-to-tick assignments and needle angles on the pilot dials; 10-26 to 10-29 pilot and gates; 10-30 to 11-06 full test runs and ablations; 11-07 to 11-09 buffer. Pilot (gating, threshold setting only): 200 MeasureBench real dials stratified by tags assigned before any run (single-pointer gauges, clocks, multi-dial meters, glare or shadow, counterweighted or tapered needles, non-linear scales), plus 150 TickTockVQA train-split clocks. Test (reported): the remaining 511 MeasureBench real dials and 1,000 randomly sampled TickTockVQA test images, never touched during development. Sizing: with a paired design, if about 30% of items are discordant between two systems the paired standard error at n = 200 is about 3.9 points, so an 8-point gap has a 95% bootstrap lower bound above zero; at the earlier n = 100 it would not (reviewer carry-forward). Pilot-gated commitments: G1, C3 with fallback beats the best Astra configuration (max over default, high, xhigh with built-in tools) on the 200 pilot dials by at least 15 points with paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0; G2, C3 beats hybrid B by at least 8 points with lower bound > 0; G3, on the 150 pilot clocks C3 beats the best Astra configuration by at least 20 points of exact-minute accuracy; G0 (component), numeral-to-major assignment is correct on at least 85% of pilot dials that have two or more detected numerals and the lattice is resolvable (coverage) on at least 70%. If G1 and G3 pass, the paper commits to the pilot's paired-bootstrap lower bound as the minimum gain on the held-out test sets. If G2 fails, the paper reports hybrid B (training-free frontier + ranked lattice + Hough needle) as the method and the needle sweep as a negative result. If G1 fails, the run stops and the failure analysis (oracle splits) is the outcome. Budget rule: per-call cost and latency are measured on the first 50 pilot images for each Astra configuration; with 1,861 images in total and four configurations, if the projected spend exceeds US$700 the xhigh-with-tools baseline is run only on the 711 dials and 300 test clocks, keeping US$300 in reserve for ablations and reruns.

falsifiable_predictions.pillar: Overall accuracy and cost change (pilot-gated, G1)
falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted, not observed: on the 511 held-out MeasureBench real dials, C3 with frontier fallback exceeds the best GPT-6 Astra configuration (including xhigh with built-in tools) by at least 15 points of value+unit accuracy, at no more than 1.2x Astra-default API cost per image.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: The pilot gain over the best Astra configuration is below 15 points or its paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound is at or below zero; or Astra xhigh with built-in tools comes within 5 points of C3 at no more than 2x C3's API cost per image.

falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: on pilot dials with two or more detected numerals, numeral-to-major assignment is correct on at least 85%, and joint ranking cuts errors of exactly one minor or one major tick by at least 40% relative to sequential rounding on the same lattice.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Assignment accuracy below 70%, or joint ranking within 2 points of sequential rounding in overall accuracy.

falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: C3 beats hybrid B by at least 8 points overall on the pilot (lower bound above zero) and by at least 15 points on the shadow/glare, counterweight, tapered-needle and multi-hand subsets, while staying within 3 points on crisp single needles.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Overall gain over hybrid B below 4 points, or nuisance-subset gain below 8 points; in that case hybrid B becomes the reported method and the sweep is reported as negative.

falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: the labelling margin detects C3's errors with AUROC at least 0.80 overall and at least 0.75 on items where Astra's three samples agree but are wrong, where Astra's verbalised confidence stays at or below 0.60 AUROC; at the pilot-fixed threshold C3 reaches at least 75% selective accuracy at coverage of at least 50%.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Margin AUROC below 0.70 overall, or selective accuracy below 65% at 50% coverage.

falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: on 1,000 TickTockVQA test images, C3 exceeds the best Astra configuration by at least 20 points of exact-minute accuracy and halves the hour/minute swap rate; removing the coupling costs at least 5 points.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: Gain below 10 points over the best Astra configuration, or coupling ablation within 2 points.

falsifiable_predictions.prediction: Predicted: a +-1 minor-tick window centred on Astra's reading loses at least 10 points on clocks and at least 5 points on dials relative to the full-range sweep, because the frontier reading is often more than one interval off.
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: The frontier-centred window matches the full-range sweep within 2 points on both sets, which would mean the frontier reading is already a valid coarse code and the extra search is unneeded.

limitations: Scope is analog dials and clocks; MeasureBench's 361 linear instruments, 96 digital and 104 composite items are not addressed, and the method needs a visible tick ring or numerals.

On low-resolution or heavily blurred photos minor ticks may not be resolvable after rectification; the method then abstains, so coverage, not accuracy, caps the gain, and the training-free rectification and lattice extraction are the stages where earlier pipelines broke [2510.26865][2404.08785].

The phase-unwrapping framing mostly re-describes ordinary tick counting because the whole lattice is visible; the substantive borrowings are joint labelling enumeration and margin-based abstention [1608.05209].

The method depends on the frontier for numeral values, units, scale type and pointer semantics; misreads of decimals, multiple overlaid scales or unusual units propagate, and the published frontier baselines are 2025 numbers until Astra is measured in the pilot.
Hand-set score weights and thresholds are fixed on a 200-dial pilot; they may not transfer to instrument families absent from MeasureBench and TickTockVQA.
